observation_summary: Adding zero units of time (days, months, years) to a MutableDateTime object during a DST transition causes an unexpected change in the time zone offset, effectively shifting the absolute time.
reasoning_summary: The bug involves an incorrect calculation or procedure when performing date arithmetic. Specifically, the implementation of addDays(0), addMonths(0), and addYears(0) incorrectly triggers a recalculation of the time zone offset during a DST overlap, even though the duration added is zero. This is a procedural error in the logic that handles date/time field manipulation, fitting the definition of an Algorithm/Method defect.
evidence_used: The bug report states that addDays(0), addMonths(0), and addYears(0) change the value of the object during a DST transition, while addHours(0) does not.
The failing tests (e.g., testAddDays_int_dstOverlapWinter_addZero) show a mismatch in the expected time zone offset (+01:00 vs +02:00) after calling addDays(0).
The issue is specific to field-based addition methods, suggesting a flaw in the underlying calculation logic for these fields.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix might involve adding a check for zero, the root cause is the incorrect implementation of the addition algorithm itself, which fails to handle the zero-addition case correctly within the context of DST transitions.
